text:
Brett Pesce is having the kind of quiet season that makes a defense work. He plays about 21 minutes a night for New Jersey, blocks shots (32 in 19 games), and the Devils take 58% of the shot attempts and 60% of the expected goals with him on the ice at five on five, five points better than when he sits. He also has 8 points, more than his whole total in 37 games last season, six of them in his last ten.

Don't read the points as a new offensive game. He has almost no shots of his own that count as chances; the assists come from being on the ice when good players score. The real value is at his own blue line: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 22% of entries aimed at him last season, double a typical rate, over a small sample of nine games. The weak spot was the other direction, with only 20% of his exits keeping the puck.

He missed the Nov. 12 game against Washington with an illness, per CBS Sports. At 32, healthy and paired in a good system, he's earning his minutes.
